worlds.village: A dosa shared by a family: cut into 4 equal pieces, each child gets 1/4 of the dosa.
worlds.city: A pizza cut into 8 slices; eating 3 slices means you ate 3/8 of it.
worlds.cricket: An over has 6 balls; after 2 balls, 2/6 (= 1/3) of the over is done.
worlds.cinema: A 3-hour film: after 1 hour you have watched 1/3 of it.
worlds.kitchen: A dosa cut into equal slices: the denominator is how many slices, the numerator how many you take.
worlds.farm: A field split into 5 equal strips; planting rice in 2 strips covers 2/5 of the field.
worlds.festivals: A box of 12 laddoos at Diwali; giving 3 to a neighbour is 3/12 = 1/4 of the box.

worlds.village: Out of 100 mango trees in the village, 25 give fruit this year: 25 percent.
worlds.city: A 20% off sale on a Rs 500 shirt takes Rs 100 off the price.
worlds.cricket: A batter who scores 60 runs off 100 balls has a strike rate of 60 percent of a run per ball.
worlds.cinema: If 75 of 100 seats in the theatre are full, the hall is 75 percent full.
worlds.kitchen: If 10 of 100 grams of dal is salt-free spice mix, that is 10 percent.
worlds.farm: If 30 of every 100 seeds do not sprout, the farmer loses 30 percent of the seeds.
worlds.festivals: A Diwali discount of 10% on Rs 1,000 of crackers saves Rs 100.

worlds.village: Mixing 1 part jaggery with 3 parts water for panakam: the ratio is 1:3.
worlds.city: A metro has 2 ladies' coaches for every 6 coaches: ratio 2:6 = 1:3.
worlds.cricket: A team wins 4 matches for every 1 it loses: the win-loss ratio is 4:1.
worlds.cinema: A film with 3 songs for every 1 fight scene has a song-fight ratio of 3:1.
worlds.kitchen: Idli batter uses 4 cups of rice for 1 cup of urad dal: ratio 4:1.
worlds.farm: Mixing 2 bags of compost for every 5 bags of soil keeps the ratio 2:5.
worlds.festivals: For rangoli, 1 cup of colour for every 2 cups of rice flour: ratio 1:2.

worlds.village: A bullock cart that covers 8 km to the market in 2 hours moves at 4 km per hour.
worlds.city: An auto-rickshaw covering 30 km in 1 hour runs at 30 km/h; in traffic it covers less in the same time.
worlds.cricket: A fast bowler's ball travels about 22 metres to the batter in under half a second.
worlds.cinema: A chase scene: the hero's bike covers more distance than the villain's jeep in the same time, so it is faster.
worlds.kitchen: Pouring a 1-litre jug in 10 seconds is faster than pouring it in 20 seconds: speed is amount per unit time.
worlds.farm: A tractor ploughing 2 acres per hour works at twice the speed of one ploughing 1 acre per hour.
worlds.festivals: A temple chariot pulled 1 km in 2 hours moves at half a km per hour.

worlds.village: The fence around a field is its perimeter; the land you can plant inside is its area.
worlds.city: The skirting along the walls of a flat is the perimeter; the floor tiles cover the area.
worlds.cricket: The boundary rope is the perimeter of the ground; the grass inside is the area.
worlds.cinema: The border lights around a screen measure the perimeter; the picture fills the area.
worlds.kitchen: The rim of a chapati tawa is its perimeter; the space where the chapati cooks is its area.
worlds.farm: Walking once around a paddy field measures its perimeter; the seedlings planted inside fill its area.
worlds.festivals: The border of a kolam is its perimeter; the coloured pattern inside covers its area.

worlds.village: A kolam drawn at the doorstep looks the same on both sides of its middle line.
worlds.city: The front of the Gateway of India is the same on the left and right of its centre.
worlds.cricket: The stumps and bails look the same from the left and the right of the middle stump.
worlds.cinema: A movie poster with the hero exactly in the centre and matching sides is symmetric.
worlds.kitchen: A round roti folded in half has two halves that match: the fold is a line of symmetry.
worlds.farm: A leaf folded along its middle vein: the two halves match.
worlds.festivals: A kolam or rangoli for Pongal or Diwali: fold it along the middle and both halves match.

worlds.village: A weighing scale at the village shop: whatever you remove from one side you must remove from the other to keep it balanced.
worlds.city: A bus ticket: total fare = fare per km x km; if you know the total and the rate, you can find the km.
worlds.cricket: Runs needed: target - runs scored = runs still needed; the unknown is the runs still needed.
worlds.cinema: Ticket money: number of tickets x price = total collection; find the tickets when you know the rest.
worlds.kitchen: A balance scale with dal on one side: take the same weight off both sides and it stays balanced.
worlds.farm: Bags of rice x weight per bag = total harvest; divide to find the number of bags.
worlds.festivals: Sweets per box x boxes = total sweets; if 60 sweets fill 5 boxes, each box has the unknown 12.

worlds.village: Current is like water flowing in a pipe from the village tank: voltage is how high the tank is, resistance is how narrow the pipe is.
worlds.city: Current is like cars on a road: voltage pushes them, a narrow road (resistance) lets fewer through.
worlds.cricket: Current is like runs flowing in: a good pitch (low resistance) lets more runs come.
worlds.cinema: Current is like the crowd flowing through a theatre gate: a narrow gate (resistance) slows the flow.
worlds.kitchen: Current is like water from a tap: open the tap wider (less resistance) and more flows.
worlds.farm: Current is like water in an irrigation pipe: a pump (voltage) pushes it, a narrow pipe (resistance) slows it.
worlds.festivals: Diwali serial lights in one circuit: if one bulb breaks, the path is broken and the current stops.

worlds.village: The monsoon: the sun heats the ponds, the vapour forms clouds, and the rain refills the village tank.
worlds.city: Water on a hot road dries up (evaporates), rises into clouds and falls again as monsoon rain.
worlds.cricket: Covers on the pitch get droplets after a humid night: water vapour condensing, like clouds forming.
worlds.cinema: The rain song in a film starts with the sea, the sun and the clouds: that is the water cycle.
worlds.kitchen: Steam from a boiling pot hits the lid and drips back down: evaporation, condensation and 'rain'.
worlds.farm: The monsoon brings rain to the fields, the sun dries the water, and it returns as clouds.
worlds.festivals: Onam and Pongal follow the monsoon harvest: rain from clouds that formed from evaporated sea water.

worlds.village: A leaf is a small kitchen: it takes sunlight, water and air (carbon dioxide) and cooks sugar for the plant.
worlds.city: Rooftop plants work like solar panels: they use sunlight to make their food.
worlds.cricket: The grass on the outfield stays green by making food from sunlight, water and air.
worlds.cinema: A plant is like a film studio powered by sunlight: the leaves are where the food is produced.
worlds.kitchen: A leaf cooks sugar using sunlight as its stove, water and carbon dioxide as ingredients.
worlds.farm: Paddy leaves use sunlight, water from the field and carbon dioxide to make the grain's food.
worlds.festivals: Mango leaves on a toran stay green while fresh because they were making food from sunlight.

worlds.village: A coconut floats in the pond but a stone sinks: the stone packs more mass into the same space.
worlds.city: A full steel tiffin is heavier than a plastic one of the same size: steel is denser.
worlds.cricket: A leather cricket ball is heavier than a tennis ball of similar size: it is denser.
worlds.cinema: In films, styrofoam 'rocks' float because their density is much lower than real rock.
worlds.kitchen: Oil floats on water in the pan because oil is less dense than water.
worlds.farm: Light chaff floats away when grain is winnowed; dense grain falls straight down.
worlds.festivals: Diyas floated on the river at festivals stay up because they are less dense than water.

worlds.village: If three families give 2, 4 and 6 kg of rice to the temple, the average is (2 + 4 + 6) / 3 = 4 kg.
worlds.city: Your average bus fare over a week is the total fare divided by the number of trips.
worlds.cricket: A batting average is total runs divided by the number of times the batter got out.
worlds.cinema: A film's average daily collection is the total collection divided by the days it ran.
worlds.kitchen: If three batches of idlis take 10, 12 and 14 minutes, the average is 12 minutes.
worlds.farm: Average yield per acre is the total harvest divided by the number of acres.
worlds.festivals: If you burst 10, 20 and 30 crackers over three nights, the average is 20 per night.
